subject: Context & output sizing for pricing — follow-up and Anchor
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
To: Maya Singh <maya@atlasretail.com>, Tom Brooks <tom@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Context & output sizing for pricing — recap + a few asks

Hi Maya / Tom,

Great to chat this morning — thanks for walking through Atlas Retail's planned features. Quick recap and two asks so we can line up an accurate pricing anchor: 

Recap (from what I captured):
- Primary feature: personalized product descriptions + chat support inside merchant admin.
- Typical session flow: prompt (user query + product metadata) -> model completion -> light post-processing.
- Expected peak concurrency: ~1200 requests/minute during promos, steady-state ~150 reqs/min.
- Desired latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms for completion tokens.

What I need from you to finalize a $/1M-tokens anchor:
1) Average prompt tokens and average completion tokens (either overall or per feature). If you have a small sample export, attach it (CSV is great).
2) Rough distribution of context length needs: what percent of requests need 8k vs 32k vs 128k context windows? Even coarse buckets help.
3) Monthly budget range (ballpark) or target unit economics — you mentioned a target ~$X per 1M tokens last week; can you confirm a target range?

To make it easier, I attached a tiny sample CSV template and a draft pricing anchor we'll use as baseline. If you prefer, reply with the sample and we'll run model-cost estimates and recommended capacity (hosted vs dedicated).

Next steps I propose:
- You: send sample export + context distribution (items 1–2 above) by EOD Wed (May 19)
- Us: return an initial pricing anchor and 3-month cost projection by Fri (May 21)

Attachments: [atlas_usage_sample.csv (CSV), redwood_pricing_anchor.pdf (PDF draft)]

Thanks —
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Maya Singh <maya@atlasretail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Cc: Tom Brooks <tom@atlasretail.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 12:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Context & output sizing for pricing — recap + a few asks

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the clear notes. Attached is a small export from last month's traffic (sanitized): it has one row per request with columns: feature, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, context_window_used. Quick answers inline: 

1) Averages (overall): avg prompt tokens = 980, avg completion tokens = 420.
2) Context distribution (estimates): 8k: 86%, 32k: 12%, 128k: 2%. The 128k cases are deep product history + cross-merchant analysis and are rare.
3) Budget / target: we're aiming for a cost target of $600 / 1M tokens as an internal threshold for the first 6 months. Monthly budget band we can commit to is roughly $8k–$30k depending on conversion in the pilot.

Notes: the 32k cases increase during weekly merchandising updates where we send larger catalogs as context. Attached file: atlas_usage_sample.csv.

Tom — looping you for procurement timeline.

Best,
Maya
VP Product | Atlas Retail
maya@atlasretail.com | +1 212 555 0134

[Attachment: atlas_usage_sample.csv]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Maya Singh <maya@atlasretail.com>, Tom Brooks <tom@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 14:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Context & output sizing for pricing — recap + a few asks

Maya — thanks for the quick data, super helpful. A few clarifying questions so our cost model maps correctly to your usage profile: 

- The avg prompt tokens of ~980: is that inclusive of cached prefixes (e.g., product metadata you can cache per session) or is that full serialized input each time? If you can mark which columns are cacheable in the CSV that helps.
- For the 12% 32k cases: is that primarily larger single-request contexts (one big catalog) or multiple smaller attachments concatenated?
- Do the 128k requests contain long-running KV caches (benefit from prefix caching) or are they unique at each call?

Initial interpretive notes (back-of-envelope):
- Given ~1k prompt + 0.42k completion avg, the effective token mix is ~70% prompt / 30% completion by token count.
- At your $600 / 1M token target, monthly tokens budget that fits $8k–$30k would be ~13.3M–50M tokens/month.

Ben and I will run two pricing anchors: hosted (usage) and a dedicated-reserved option with quantized models (8-bit/4-bit) and prefix caching assumptions. Expect a short note by tomorrow with $/1M examples and a recommended capacity path (pilot -> scale).

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[karthik.iyer@redwood.inference]
From: Tom Brooks <tom@atlasretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@atlasretail.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:19:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Context & output sizing for pricing — recap + a few asks

Thanks Karthik — quick answers: 
- Prompt caching: yes — product metadata is cacheable for ~90% of requests (we can provide a flag in the logs).
- 32k cases: usually a single large catalog blob we attach to the prompt (one-off for weekly updates).
- 128k cases: unique and not cacheable (deep analysis runs), but again only 2% of calls and mostly during monthly reports.

Procurement note: target timeline for a pilot contract is mid-June. Procurement will need SOC2, terms sheet, and a simple POC acceptance test plan.

Tom
Head of Engineering | Atlas Retail
[t] +1 212 555 0167
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Maya Singh <maya@atlasretail.com>, Tom Brooks <tom@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Context & output sizing for pricing — recap + a few asks

Maya / Tom — appreciate the details. Based on the sample and clarifications here is our initial pricing-anchor summary (top-line only):

Scenarios (approx):
1) Hosted (fully managed): baseline model (float16), no heavy quantization, with prefix caching applied: ~ $1,050 / 1M tokens. This assumes your cacheable prompts reduce prompt token throughput by ~45%.
2) Hosted + recommended batching/caching tweaks: ~$780 / 1M tokens (aggressive batching and prefix cache hit ops).
3) Dedicated reserved + 8-bit quantized model (recommended for predictable mid-volume): ~$420 / 1M tokens — but requires a 3–6 month reserved commitment and expected ~30% perf uplift on cost.

Given your $600 / 1M target and the 13–50M token monthly window we estimated:
- Pilot recommendation: start hosted with caching/batching optimizations for 6–8 weeks to validate quality and latency during your promo cadence. If peak cost or latency becomes binding, transition to dedicated quantized nodes in month 3.

Requested next steps from Atlas for a precise quote:
- Confirm cacheable flag in logs (Tom to provide sample column) — this will materially change prompt token costing.
- Confirm pilot volume commitment band (e.g., 15–25M tokens for month 1) so we can price reserved options properly.
- Procurement checklist: we'll send SOC2 summary + terms sheet + simple POC test plan within 24 hours.

I'll attach the short anchor deck and a worked example that maps your 980/420 mix to monthly $ estimates across scenarios.

Best,
Ben Carter
Lead Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference | +1 650 555 0110
